messages.author: 2cbe10bd251e661a
messages.subject: Is there any way to produce multiple plot panels other than with  facet?
parts:
Facet is a bit inflexible, e.g., if you want to plot multiple data
sets in subpanels of a single display. Is there a way to do this more
procedurally, addressing each panel / facet separately?

messages.author: b26ea422f70d3a1f
messages.subject: Re: Is there any way to produce multiple plot panels other than with facet?
parts:
First, a facetious answer I just couldn't resists: It's called lattice.

Seriously, though, to simply plot separate data sets in subpanels of a
single display, you can join your sub data sets into one data frame,
with a new dummy variable to indicate which data set each entry is
from. Then use this dummy variable to facet. Or do I misunderstand the
task?

Wayne

>

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Is there any way to produce multiple plot panels other than with  facet?
parts:
You can use grid.layout to place several ggplots on the same page.
There is however a difficulty if you want them to have a common axis
for example. I'm not aware of any obvious trick to make sure the plots
are aligned and of the same size, for instance (latticeExtra has the
c.trellis method for this). Is this what you have in mind?

baptiste

qplot(block, value, data = rm, colour = var, facets = . ~ type)

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Is there any way to produce multiple plot panels other than with  facet?
parts:
What should I do if the two plots are based on completely different
geoms?

I would like to draw PlotA on top of PlotB on top of a shared time
axis, where PlotA is the queue length as a function of time, and PlotB
is related to queue utilization and drops. I have developed custom
geoms to plot these two things nicely (for example, I sample queue
size to reduce the number of plot points, then I draw a line for
sampled queue size as well as a polygon to show the minimum and
maximum; for PlotB I shade in certain areas on the plot that can be
interpreted as amount of idleness and amount of drops).

In lattice, I can call xyplot, and tell it to use a custom panel
function for each of the two plots. In ggplot2, how do I tell it to
use different geoms for the two panels?

Damon.

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Is there any way to produce multiple plot panels other than with  facet?
parts:
Try this perhaps,

dummy <- data.frame(x=seq(1, 10, length=100), y=rnorm(100),
type=factor(c("f1", "f2")))

d1 <- data.frame(x=1:10, y=sin(1:10), type="f1")
d2 <- data.frame(x=1:10, y=cos(1:10), type="f2")

ggplot(data = dummy, mapping = aes(x = x, y = y)) +
facet_grid(type~., scale="free") +
layer(data=d1, geom = c( "line"), stat = "identity" ) +
layer(data=d2, geom = c( "point"), stat = "identity" )

baptiste
